method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **May be an asymptomatic laboratory finding. Stop any oral or IV phosphate-containing products.** ⚠️ **Assess for acute or chronic renal impairment if severe; seek specialist advice if symptomatic.**
claims.source_text: Hyperphosphataemia may be an asymptomatic laboratory finding Cease any oral or intravenous products that contain phosphate Assess for renal impairment (acute or chronic) in the presence of severe hyperphosphataemia Specialist advice should be sought for symptomatic children with hyperphosphataemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pseudo-hyperphosphataemia** can follow ex vivo haemolysis, e.g. a difficult draw or tourniquet.
claims.source_text: Pseudo-hyperphosphataemia may result from ex vivo haemolysis eg due to difficult blood sampling/tourniquet
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check renal function (urine output, UEC), calcium and albumin.** ⚠️ **Severe hyperphosphataemia can cause symptomatic hypocalcaemia.**
claims.source_text: Assess renal function (urine output, serum urea, electrolytes and creatinine) and check serum calcium and albumin levels. Severe hyperphosphataemia can lead to symptomatic hypocalcaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check the sample:** timing against recent IV phosphate and whether it was drawn from the infusion's IV access; **repeat if haemolysis is suspected.**
claims.source_text: Check timing of blood sampling in relation to recent intravenous phosphate infusions and whether the sample was taken from the same intravenous access as where the infusion was administered Repeat test if there is a clinical suspicion of sample haemolysis related to difficult blood sampling
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about phosphate-containing medicines and supplements, including enemas.**
claims.source_text: Ask about medications and supplements that may contain phosphate, including enemas
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Often asymptomatic in isolation.** Features: anorexia, nausea, vomiting · kidney failure · tachycardia, arrhythmia, ECG changes · weakness or spasms, hyperreflexia, soft-tissue and vascular calcification · secondary hyperparathyroidism.
claims.source_text: Hyperphosphataemia in isolation is often asymptomatic Gastrointestinal: anorexia, nausea, vomiting Renal: acute or chronic kidney failure Cardiac: tachycardia, arrhythmias, ECG changes Neuromuscular: muscle weakness or spasms, hyperreflexia, soft tissue and vascular calcifications Endocrine: secondary hyperparathyroidism
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor phosphate at a frequency set by the degree of abnormality and symptoms.**
claims.source_text: Serum phosphate levels should be monitored, with frequency depending on the degree of the abnormality and whether the child is symptomatic
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat the cause, aiming for the normal range;** monitor clinically and with phosphate and calcium. **Stop phosphate-containing medicines or IV solutions.**
claims.source_text: Treatment should be directed at the underlying cause with an aim to return serum phosphate levels to the normal range. Monitor closely with clinical and biochemical (serum phosphate and calcium levels) parameters Cease any phosphate containing medications or intravenous solutions
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Significant acute: promote renal excretion with IV sodium chloride 0.9% volume expansion or a loop diuretic.** ⚠️ **Caution with renal impairment — discuss with nephrology or PICU.**
claims.source_text: In significant acute hyperphosphataemia, renal phosphate excretion can be encouraged by extracellular volume expansion with intravenous sodium chloride 0.9% or use of loop diuretic agent (Use caution if acute or chronic renal impairment is present. Discuss with local nephrology or PICU team)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe or symptomatic, particularly with kidney injury, may need dialysis — discuss with nephrology or PICU.**
claims.source_text: Children with severe or symptomatic hyperphosphataemia, particularly those with acute or chronic kidney injury, may require dialysis. Discuss with local nephrology or PICU team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Chronic: dietary phosphorus restriction and/or phosphate binders such as calcium carbonate.**
claims.source_text: Chronic hyperphosphataemia may require dietary phosphorus restriction and/or use of phosphate binding agents eg calcium carbonate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Paediatric team** if symptomatic or significantly abnormal; **renal team** if renal dysfunction; **consider transfer** if symptomatic or needing monitoring your centre cannot provide.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when The child is symptomatic or there is a significant abnormality Consider consultation with renal team when Renal dysfunction is present Consider transfer when The child is symptomatic or requires close monitoring not available in your centre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperphosphataemia' (Last updated January 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperphosphataemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
